info.title: Running Tracker HTTP API
info.description: Ordinary HTTP transport contract from SDD section 11. The /live SSE protocol is specified separately in packages/contracts/sse.md.

201.description: Session created. The opaque session is set in an HttpOnly cookie.

get.summary: Read the current session
get.description: Sessions are stored in PostgreSQL and survive an API restart until their original expiry (ADR-0080). 401 AUTH_REQUIRED means the session is unknown, signed out or expired. 503 SESSION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE (with Retry-After) means the store could not be asked: no access is granted, the cookie is left alone, and the client should keep its last confirmed session and ask again. The same 503 can answer any session-authenticated route.

delete.description: Answers 204 and clears the cookie only after the revocation is committed; from then on every API instance on the same database refuses the session. 503 SESSION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE means the revocation could not be committed: the cookie is not cleared and the session may still be valid, so the client must not report a sign-out.

get.summary: Start OpenID Connect sign-in (browser navigation)
get.description: Mounted only when OIDC is configured; otherwise 404. Meant to be followed by a browser, not called with fetch: it answers a redirect to the identity provider (authorization code, PKCE S256, state, nonce) and sets the short-lived HttpOnly login cookie scoped to /api/auth.

Set-Cookie.description: running_tracker_login: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/auth, bounded lifetime.

503.description: IDENTITY_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, or LOGIN_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE when too many sign-ins are pending or the pending-login store cannot answer (then with Retry-After).

get.summary: Complete OpenID Connect sign-in (provider redirect target)
get.description: Mounted only when OIDC is configured; otherwise 404. The identity provider sends the browser here. The pending login is stored in the shared database, so it completes after an API restart or on another API instance with the same configuration until it expires. It is single use (consumed before the provider is contacted) and its cookie is always cleared. Only an identity already provisioned as <issuer>|<subject> signs in; nobody is created.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) is set and the page navigates to the application. A 200 page rather than a redirect, because a redirect chain started from the provider would not carry the Strict cookie.

302.description: Not signed in. Redirect to the application with sign_in_error set to exactly one of denied, login_expired (no such pending login, already used, or expired), not_provisioned or unavailable (provider, session store or pending-login store could not answer; start a new sign-in).

get.summary: Process liveness
Database readiness

200.description: The API and database are ready.

get.summary: List the organizations the current identity belongs to
get.description: The identity comes only from the session; there is no way to ask about another user. Returns the organizations in which the identity has an active membership, ordered by organization id, at most 100. A person with no active membership gets an empty list, not an error. Only identifiers are returned: this is discovery, and every request that follows is still checked against the membership inside its own transaction.

get.summary: List the active coaches of the organization
get.description: For choosing whom to share a run with. The caller must have an active membership in the organization. Returns the user ids of the other active coaches in this organization, ordered by id, at most 100; runners, inactive members, other organizations and the caller are never listed. No query parameters are accepted.

get.summary: List visible runs by started-at half-open interval
Search the signed-in person's own finished runs
get.description: Owner-only: the owner is the session's identity and is not a parameter, and a run that was only shared with the person is never returned (unlike the run list). Only finished runs with a current published summary are items; a finished run in the period whose summary is missing or was computed from an older data revision is counted in `pendingSummaryCount` instead, before any distance filter. The period is a preset or an inclusive range of local calendar dates in the given IANA time zone, converted by the server to a half-open UTC interval over `started_at` (a local day is not always 24 hours). `this-month` and `previous-month` are whole calendar months in that zone, relative to the server clock. Distance bounds are decimals in `distanceUnit` (kilometres, or international miles of 1609.344 m), at most three fraction digits, and are compared inclusively with the stored metres, not with a rounded display value. Pages use a keyset cursor that is bound to the person, organization and every filter; a cursor from another query is a 400 INVALID_CURSOR. This path is registered before `/runs/{runId}`.

post.summary: Propose "My runs" search filters from a sentence (English or Russian)
post.description: Optional and off by default. Sends the text, and nothing else about the person, to the configured language model provider once; the answer is a proposal for the filter form, never a search: the caller reviews it and then calls the search endpoint above. `search` is a complete replacement filter set already checked against the search contract (the time zone is the request's, not the model's; a preset is resolved by the server clock when the search runs; the sort is `newest` when the text names none). `clarify` and `unsupported` carry only a bounded reason code, and the caller owns the wording. A condition that the search cannot express exactly (a strict distance bound, a place, a pace) is never dropped or approximated. Nothing is stored. Failures: 503 INTERPRETATION_DISABLED when the feature is off, 429 INTERPRETATION_RATE_LIMITED or INTERPRETATION_IN_PROGRESS (Retry-After where known), 503 INTERPRETATION_BUSY or INTERPRETATION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, 504 INTERPRETATION_TIMEOUT, and 502 INTERPRETATION_FAILED with `details.reason` for a refusal, an incomplete or invalid answer or a provider error. A provider refusal is a failure here, not an `unsupported` answer. The membership is checked before the provider is contacted and again before the answer is returned; no database connection is held while the provider works. Every accepted request that reaches the provider is billable, so clients must not retry automatically.

200.description: A proposal, a clarification or an unsupported reason.
Existing run returned for an equivalent retry.

get.summary: Read a visible run
List the signed-in person's own activities, newest first
get.description: Owner-only health data (ADR-0072): the owner is the session's identity and is never a parameter; coaches and other members never see another person's activities, whatever run sharing grants they hold. Ordered by `startedAt` descending, then activity id descending. `limit` 1 to 50, default 20. The keyset cursor is bound to the person and organization; a tampered or foreign cursor is a 400 INVALID_CURSOR. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

put.summary: Create an idempotent client-identified manual activity
put.description: The id is a client-generated UUID, and `idempotencyKey` is a client-generated UUID per form session, unique per owner in the organization (ADR-0073). 201 when created; 200 with the stored activity when the same id is sent again with an equal payload and key (omitted and null optional fields are equal); 409 ACTIVITY_CONFLICT when the id already holds a different payload or key. When the key already created an activity under another id: 200 with that activity if the details are equal (its `activityId` is then not the one in the path), otherwise 409 ACTIVITY_ALREADY_SAVED with `details.activityId` naming the saved activity; the details sent are not saved. An id that belongs to another member answers 404 ACTIVITY_NOT_FOUND, the same as runs. `startedAt` must not be before 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z or more than 24 hours after server time. Unknown fields are refused; the source is always `manual`.

200.description: Existing activity returned for an equivalent retry.

get.summary: Read one of the signed-in person's activities
get.description: Anyone else's activity, or an unknown id, is 404 ACTIVITY_NOT_FOUND. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Delete one of the signed-in person's activities
delete.description: A permanent hard delete without a tombstone. 204 in every case: deleted now, already deleted, never existed, or another member's (which is left untouched). The erasure is recorded in the erasure ledger in the same statement and exported off the database host, so a restored backup is cleaned by `restore:reapply-erasures` (ADR-0073). If the ledger cannot be written the deletion is not performed and the request fails (5xx); retrying is safe.

get.summary: List the signed-in person's own daily check-ins in a date range
get.description: Owner-only health data (ADR-0074): the owner is the session's identity and is never a parameter; coaches and other members never see another person's check-ins, whatever run sharing grants they hold. `from` and `to` are inclusive local dates (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01, `from` not after `to`, at most 92 days. Only days with a record are returned, ordered by `localDate` ascending. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The days with a record in the range.

put.summary: Create or fully replace the signed-in person's check-in for one local date
put.description: Naturally idempotent: the body is the whole day, so sending it again changes nothing (not even `updatedAt`). Omitted and null value fields are equal and clear the field; at least one value is required. 201 when the day is first written, 200 when it is replaced or unchanged. `timeZone` is the IANA zone the person is in now: `localDate` must not be before 2000-01-01 nor after today in that zone by server time (400 INVALID_REQUEST). The zone is stored with the day when it is first written and never rewritten, also not when a later replacement or the person uses another zone (ADR-0074). Unknown fields are refused.

200.description: The day was replaced, or already held these values.

201.description: The day was written for the first time.

get.summary: Read the signed-in person's check-in for one local date
get.description: A day without a record is 404 DAILY_METRICS_NOT_FOUND; so is anyone else's. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Delete the signed-in person's check-in for one local date
delete.description: A permanent hard delete. 204 in every case: deleted now, already deleted, never written, or a date in the future. The erasure is recorded in the erasure ledger in the same statement and exported off the database host, so a restored backup is cleaned by `restore:reapply-erasures` (ADR-0073). If the ledger cannot be written the deletion is not performed and the request fails (5xx); retrying is safe.

get.summary: List the signed-in person's own manually entered movement days in a date range
get.description: Owner-only health data (ADR-0078): the owner is the session's identity and is never a parameter; coaches, other members and run-sharing grantees never see another person's movement. `from` and `to` are inclusive local dates (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01, `from` not after `to`, at most 92 days (the daily metrics bounds). Only days with a record are returned, ordered by `localDate` ascending. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, errors included.

200.description: The days with a record in the range.

put.summary: Create or fully replace the signed-in person's manual movement for one local date
put.description: Steps and user-reported active energy (kcal, one decimal; not resting energy, total expenditure or food intake; never estimated from steps). Naturally idempotent: the body is the whole day, so sending it again changes nothing (not even `updatedAt`). Omitted and null are equal and mean "not recorded"; a 0 is a recorded value; at least one value is required. 201 when the day is first written, 200 when it is replaced or unchanged. The provenance (`source: manual`) is set by the server: a request cannot name an owner, an organization or a source (unknown fields are refused). `timeZone` is the IANA zone the person is in now: `localDate` must not be before 2000-01-01 nor after today in that zone by server time (400 INVALID_REQUEST). The zone is stored with the day when it is first written and never rewritten (ADR-0074 rules).

200.description: The day was replaced, or already held these values.

201.description: The day was written for the first time.

get.summary: Read the signed-in person's manual movement for one local date
get.description: A day without a record is 404 DAILY_MOVEMENT_NOT_FOUND; so is anyone else's. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

delete.summary: Delete the signed-in person's manual movement for one local date
delete.description: A permanent hard delete. 204 in every case: deleted now, already deleted, never written, or a date in the future. The erasure is recorded in the erasure ledger in the same statement (entity type `daily_movement`) and exported off the database host, so a restored backup is cleaned by `restore:reapply-erasures` (ADR-0073, ADR-0078). If the ledger cannot be written the deletion is not performed and the request fails (5xx); retrying is safe. A day written again after a deletion is a new record version that the old erasure cannot delete.

get.summary: List the signed-in person's own meal entries of one local date, in the order they were logged
get.description: Owner-only health data (ADR-0083): the owner is the session's identity and is never a parameter; coaches, other members and run-sharing grantees never see another person's meals. `localDate` is a local calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01. Ordered by creation instant, then id. `limit` 1 to 50, default 20. The keyset cursor is bound to the person, the organization and the date; a tampered or foreign cursor is a 400 INVALID_CURSOR. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, errors included.

200.description: One page of the date's entries.

post.summary: Log a meal or snack by hand, idempotently per form session
post.description: The id is generated by the database. `idempotencyKey` is a client-generated UUID per form session, unique per owner in the organization (ADR-0073 pattern): 201 when created; 200 with the entry when the same key is sent again with the same request (the creation request, also after the entry was edited; omitted and null values are equal, 12.50 equals 12.5); 409 MEAL_ALREADY_SAVED with `details.mealId` when the key already created an entry from a different request, and nothing is stored. A deleted entry frees its key. Nutrition values are the person's totals for the whole entry, each optional (a title-only entry is valid): null is unknown, 0 is a recorded zero; at most one decimal, refused (never rounded) otherwise. `localDate` must not be before 2000-01-01 nor after today in `timeZone` by server time (400 INVALID_REQUEST); the zone is stored as the zone of the first write. Unknown fields are refused; the source is always `manual`. Nothing is looked up, parsed, estimated or interpreted. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, errors included.

200.description: The entry this form session already created, for an equal retry.

get.summary: Read one of the signed-in person's meal entries
get.description: Anyone else's entry, or an unknown id, is 404 MEAL_NOT_FOUND. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

put.summary: Replace the editable fields of one of the signed-in person's meal entries
put.description: Replaces the meal type, the title and the four nutrition values (omitted and null are equal and clear a value). The date, the zone of the first write, the id and `createdAt` cannot be changed; a request naming them is refused. Naturally idempotent: sending the same body again changes nothing, not even `updatedAt`. Anyone else's entry, or an unknown id, is 404 MEAL_NOT_FOUND.

delete.summary: Delete one of the signed-in person's meal entries
delete.description: A permanent hard delete. 204 in every case: deleted now, already deleted, never existed, or another member's (which is left untouched). The erasure is recorded in the erasure ledger in the same statement (entity type `meal`, identifiers and version only, never the title or a value) and exported off the database host, so a restored backup is cleaned by `restore:reapply-erasures` (ADR-0073, ADR-0083). If the ledger cannot be written the deletion is not performed and the request fails (5xx); retrying is safe. An entry logged again after a deletion is a new record version that the old erasure cannot delete.

get.summary: Compute the signed-in person's overview of one local date (Today)
get.description: Owner-only derived health data (ADR-0082), computed by the app on every read and never stored; no language model is called, nothing is queued and nothing is written. Every source is read in one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction with row-level security and explicit organization and owner predicates; run sharing never adds another person's data. `localDate` must not be before 2000-01-01 nor after today in `timeZone` by server time (400 INVALID_REQUEST). Attribution: the check-in and the manually entered movement are those stored for `localDate` (their own calendar date), whatever zone they were saved in; their stored zone is returned and they are never moved to another date. Manual activities and GPS runs count on the date on which they started in `timeZone`: from that date's local midnight up to, not including, the next date's local midnight (23 or 25 hours around a daylight saving change). The response holds the check-in's values, whether it exists (a note-only check-in exists; the note text is never returned) and its stored zone; the movement values, whether they exist, their source (`manual`) and stored zone; manual activity counts and the full entered duration of the activities that started on the date (also of one that continued past midnight), by type; and the person's own finished GPS runs: their count, how many have a distance from a summary current for the run's data, and the sum of those distances only (a partial total covers exactly the `withCurrentDistance` runs). Manual activities and GPS runs are reported separately (they may describe the same session) and movement is never added to either. A value that was not recorded is null, never zero. No raw GPS points, notes or other free text. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, errors included.

get.summary: Compute the signed-in person's 28-day trends of four daily series
get.description: Owner-only derived health data (ADR-0084), computed by the app on every read and never stored; no language model is called, nothing is queued and nothing is written. Every source is read in one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction with row-level security and explicit organization and owner predicates, by a fixed set of range statements; run sharing never adds another person's data. The range is the 28 calendar dates ending on `endDate` inclusive; when 2000-01-01 cuts it short, the response gives the actual first date and number of dates (`range.days`, the denominator of every coverage figure) and `shortenedByLowerBound: true`. `endDate` must not be after today in `timeZone` by server time (400 INVALID_REQUEST); `timeZone` decides only that, never a record's date. Every record belongs to the calendar date it was stored for, whatever zone it was saved in. Four series, one entry per date: recorded weight (kg) and sleep duration (minutes) from the check-in, manually entered steps from the movement record, and food energy from the logged meal entries (entries logged, entries with energy, and the exact sum over those entries, or null when none records energy). A value that was not recorded is null, never zero, and adds nothing to any total or average; a recorded 0 is a value. The summary is defined by `summarizeDailyTrendDays`: weight's first, last and change only with at least two recorded dates; the sleep average over recorded dates only, rounded to the nearest minute with halves up; the recorded step total with its day count; the recorded food-energy total with both its day and its entry coverage. Food energy is never described as a complete diary: unlogged food is unknown. No note text, meal titles, other free text, balance, target, prediction or advice. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, errors included.

get.summary: Compute the signed-in person's weekly review
get.description: Owner-only derived health data, computed by the app on every read and never stored. No language model is called and nothing is queued: the review works whether AI generation (WEEKLY_INSIGHTS_PROVIDER) is on or off and whether or not an AI insight exists for the week. Every source of the week (the person's own check-ins, manual activities and finished GPS runs; never anyone else's runs, even when run sharing makes them readable) is read in one statement of one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction, so a source deleted before the read began is absent. The week runs Monday to Sunday in the time zone stored on the person's check-ins in that week (the most frequent one), or in `timeZone` when there are none; a week starting after today in `timeZone` is refused (400 INVALID_REQUEST). The response carries the week and its effective zone; per-metric coverage with explicit denominators (days in the week, days with numeric check-in values, days with each metric; a note-only check-in is not a day with values, and a sleep-quality rating never counts as a recorded sleep duration); the facts (a value that was not recorded has no fact, never a zero; a GPS distance only from summaries current for the run's data, with the runs it covers); code-written descriptive statements with stable codes; data gaps and source limitations; and provenance (`source: computed_by_app`, `persisted: false`, the review and aggregation policy versions and the computation time), which distinguishes it from a stored AI insight (that has a model, a prompt version, an id and a creation time). Manual runs and GPS runs are never added together. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Ask for the signed-in person's weekly insight
post.description: Owner-only derived health data (ADR-0076). The server computes the week's numbers (check-in coverage, sleep, mood, soreness, weight, manual activities by type, GPS runs reported separately from manual runs, with a GPS distance only from a summary that is current for the run's data) from the person's own records and publishes them as facts; free-text notes, coordinates and identifiers are never sent to the model. A local language model writes prose without numbers, days or dates and cites facts as claims; the server discards any answer that is not the schema, whose claims do not equal the facts in value, unit, direction and day, or whose prose contains a number, a day or a date (failed_grounding), or that contains medical content or advice to ignore symptoms or avoid help (failed_safety). In a week with extreme soreness or sleep the suggestion is chosen by code from a fixed non-medical set. The week runs Monday to Sunday in the time zone stored on the person's check-ins in that week, or in `timeZone` when there are none; a week starting after today in `timeZone` is refused (400 INVALID_REQUEST). Answers 202 at once with `queued` (or the existing insight's status); generation runs in the background, one at a time per server, within a total time and attempt budget, and the result is read with GET. The same computed data, model, prompt and policy version return the existing insight; a different input replaces the week's insight. Asking again retries an `interrupted` or `generation_failed` insight, at most 3 attempts per input (then 409 WEEKLY_INSIGHT_RETRY_LIMIT); a `failed_grounding` or `failed_safety` result is returned as it is until the data changes. Deleting or changing a source record deletes the insights of the affected week in the same transaction, and a request can never store an insight about sources that changed after it read them. 503 WEEKLY_INSIGHTS_DISABLED when no model is configured, 503 WEEKLY_INSIGHTS_BUSY when the generation queue is full (nothing is stored then). Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

202.description: Accepted, or the existing insight for the same input; read it with GET.

get.summary: Read the signed-in person's insight for one week
get.description: The week's insight with its status and freshness. The server recomputes the week's input from the current data on every read: `freshness` is `current` when it equals the insight's input, `stale` when the data changed since (the output is still returned, marked out of date), and `outdated_policy` when the insight was validated under an older policy (its output is withheld). A `queued` or `running` insight whose lease has expired (a restart lost its job) is reported as `interrupted`. `output` is present only for a `ready` insight under the current policy; a failed status never carries model output. A week without an insight (never asked, or deleted together with a source record), and anyone else's, is 404 WEEKLY_INSIGHT_NOT_FOUND. Readable also when generation is disabled. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: Apply or replay an idempotent lifecycle command

get.summary: Read raw point history
List the shares of an owned run
get.description: Owner only: anyone else, a grantee included, gets the same answer as for a missing run. Each item carries both permission flags as stored, ordered by grantee id, at most 100; `truncated` is true when more exist. No query parameters are accepted.

put.summary: Create or replace an owned run share

get.summary: Read a stable initial live-track page
Read a stable live-track change page
get.description: Exactly one of afterRevision or cursor is required.

get.summary: Read published archive geometry
get.description: Finished runs only, under active membership and history authorization. One statement snapshot returns a GeoJSON Feature with run metadata and pending/stale/ready summary state. Only ready carries metrics and geometry; null geometry in ready is a valid empty track. Reads published summaries even after raw purge. Source revision equality determines readiness; algorithmVersion identifies the published algorithm. Private/no-store, at most 1 MiB UTF-8 JSON and 100,000 vertices; oversized tracks fail without truncation.

200.description: GeoJSON Feature with explicit summary state.

422.description: ARCHIVE_TRACK_TOO_COMPLEX: response exceeds 1 MiB or 100,000 vertices.

get.summary: List visible archive runs intersecting a WGS84 bbox
get.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Specified in SDD section 11 but not mounted by the service; the request is answered 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND. Archive display uses /archive/metadata and the revision-bound /tiles instead; live positions come from the /live stream.

get.summary: Read confirmed fresh nearby run positions
get.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Specified in SDD section 11 but not mounted by the service; the request is answered 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND. Archive display uses /archive/metadata and the revision-bound /tiles instead; live positions come from the /live stream.

get.summary: Read revisioned archive tile metadata
Read a revision-bound Mapbox Vector Tile

200.description: A Mapbox Vector Tile; an empty result is a valid empty MVT.

MealLocalDate.name: localDate
MealLocalDate.description: The local calendar date whose entries are listed (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01.

DailyMetricsFrom.name: from
DailyMetricsFrom.description: First local date of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01.

DailyMetricsTo.name: to
DailyMetricsTo.description: Last local date of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Not before `from`; at most 92 days from it.

WeekStart.name: weekStart
WeekStart.description: The Monday the week starts on, as a local calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD), not before 2000-01-01.

ReviewTimeZone.name: timeZone
ReviewTimeZone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Europe/Warsaw. Decides the week's days only when the person has no check-in in that week; otherwise the zone stored on their check-ins does.

OverviewTimeZone.name: timeZone
OverviewTimeZone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Europe/Warsaw. Decides "today" and the interval in which manual activities and GPS runs started; check-ins and movement keep their stored date.

TrendsEndDate.name: endDate
TrendsEndDate.description: The last local calendar date of the range (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive; not before 2000-01-01 nor after today in `timeZone`.

TrendsTimeZone.name: timeZone
TrendsTimeZone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Europe/Warsaw. Decides "today" (the latest allowed end date) only; every record keeps its stored date.

SearchTimeZone.name: timeZone
SearchTimeZone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Europe/Warsaw. Offsets and abbreviations are refused.

SearchPreset.name: preset
SearchPreset.description: Whole calendar month in `timeZone`. Give either `preset` or both `fromDate` and `toDate`.

SearchFromDate.name: fromDate
SearchFromDate.description: First local calendar date of the period, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD).

SearchToDate.name: toDate
SearchToDate.description: Last local calendar date of the period, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). At most 366 days from `fromDate`.

SearchMaxDistance.name: maxDistance
SearchMaxDistance.description: Inclusive upper bound in `distanceUnit`. Needs `distanceUnit`; not below `minDistance`.

SearchDistanceUnit.name: distanceUnit
SearchDistanceUnit.description: Required with a distance bound and refused without one. `mi` is the international mile, 1609.344 m.

SearchSort.name: sort
SearchSort.description: Default `newest`. Ties on the sort key are ordered by newest start, then run id.

Bbox.name: bbox
Bbox.description: west,south,east,north in WGS84; west > east crosses the antimeridian.

TileX.name: x
TileX.description: XYZ x coordinate; must be less than 2^z.

TileY.name: y
TileY.description: XYZ y coordinate; must be less than 2^z.
